correctness.rationale: Both sequential argument evaluations are in I and the update preserves the state rectangle. Same-forcing secants give the matrix with rows (-A,-A) and (AB,-B(1-A)), where 0<=A<=a and 0<=B<=b. On representatives (1,0),(1,-1),(0,1) of the opposite pairs of hexagonal unit vertices, its output norms are A,B,A+B-AB; by convexity the last is exactly its norm. The componentwise-increasing maximum is q. With the state held fixed, the two forcing columns are (-A,AB) and (0,-B), of norms A and B. The mixed comparison therefore gives the stated geometric-series bound. Pullback trajectories at each k are Cauchy by comparing over the common suffix on the bounded rectangle; continuity gives the recurrence, and the same estimate gives bilateral uniqueness. Only forcing indices strictly below k enter; uniqueness gives shift equivariance and constancy at zero forcing. The unforced period follows from strict increase and endpoint signs of T-f(T)-g(T). The admissible tanh example attains the matrix bound to first order, including a zero gain by taking the corresponding map constant. The affine endpoint gives p_k=2-p_{k-1}, n_k=1 and hence a continuum of distinct two-cycles (take 0<s<=1/5). The proof is for the invariant one-lag event model; no asymptotic spectral-radius or physical realization claim follows. VERIFICATION.md and verify.py were inspected, not executed; the universal checks replay by the unit-vertex and pullback arguments above, not by the finite script.
